issues.t: ABS module can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no warning. Some owners may see the ABS warning light or smell burning from under the hood, even when the car is parked and off.
issues.why: The anti-lock brake control module can short out inside. Because it stays powered, it can start an engine-bay fire while parked or driving.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for recall 21V-160. Until the free fuse fix is done, park outdoors and away from buildings. If you smell burning or see smoke, move away from the car and call for help.

issues.t: Starter solenoid can short and catch fire (recall)
issues.sym: The car may crank slowly, fail to start, or you may smell burning from the engine bay. Often there is no warning before a short.
issues.why: Water can get into the starter solenoid and cause an electrical short, which can lead to an engine-bay fire.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for recall 24V-107. The dealer installs a free relay kit in the engine fuse box. Park outdoors and away from buildings until it's done.

issues.t: Turbo oil feed pipe can leak and start a fire (recall)
issues.sym: Oil spots under the front of the car, a burning oil smell, or smoke from under the hood.
issues.why: The oil supply pipe to the left turbocharger can wear out or have a loose seal, letting oil drip onto the hot exhaust manifold.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and leave the hood closed. Call 911 from a safe spot, even if you can't see flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Check your VIN for recalls 19V-538 and 24V-191. The dealer replaces the left turbo oil feed pipe for free.

issues.t: Windshield or rear glass may not be bonded properly (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom you'd normally notice. In a crash or over time, the glass could come loose.
issues.why: The wrong primer may have been used when the windshield and rear window were installed, so the adhesive doesn't hold as strongly as it should.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-305. A small number of cars are affected, and the dealer replaces both pieces of glass for free.

issues.t: Passenger airbag may not turn off for a child (recall)
issues.sym: The passenger airbag status light may show the airbag as on when the seat is empty or a child is sitting there.
issues.why: The passenger seat sensing system can wrongly detect an adult, so the airbag may deploy in a crash even with a child or child seat in that seat.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 18V-496 and get the free reprogramming. Until then, keep children in the back seat.

issues.t: Harsh upshifts or engine flare between gears
issues.sym: A hard shift or a quick rise in engine speed (flare) when the 8-speed automatic shifts from 2nd to 3rd, 3rd to 4th or 4th to 5th.
issues.why: Some shift solenoids inside the transmission can wear and stop controlling the clutches smoothly.
issues.next: Ask a Genesis dealer about bulletin 21-AT-010G. The usual fix is replacing the listed solenoids, not the whole transmission.

issues.t: Transmission slipping or incorrect gear ratio code
issues.sym: The engine revs up without the car speeding up, poor or slow shifts, and a check engine light with a gear ratio code.
issues.why: A clutch inside the transmission is slipping, or the transmission computer hasn't learned the shift pressures correctly.
issues.next: Have it diagnosed soon. Genesis bulletins 19-AT-012G and 19-AT-007G walk dealers through testing the clutches and loading oil pressure data into the transmission computer.

issues.t: Airbag warning light from the airbag control unit
issues.sym: The airbag (SRS) warning light comes on and stays on.
issues.why: The airbag control unit can store fault codes. Genesis says airbag operation isn't affected and has extended the warranty on this unit.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about bulletin 25-BE-001G. Genesis extended coverage of the airbag control unit to 15 years with unlimited miles, so the repair may be covered.

issues.t: Check engine light from a fuel pump module communication error
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code U0109. In some cases the engine may run poorly or stall.
issues.why: The engine computer loses communication with the fuel pump control module, often from a wiring, connector or module fault.
issues.next: Have the code read and the wiring and module checked. Dealers follow bulletin 21-FL-003G for the diagnosis.

issues.t: Oil pressure warning light at idle
issues.sym: The oil pressure light flickers or comes on at idle, then goes out once you drive. Some owners found the oil pressure switch leaking.
issues.why: A faulty or leaking oil pressure switch can send a false low-pressure signal. Real low oil pressure is also possible, so it must be checked.
issues.next: Check the oil level right away. If it's full, have a shop test actual oil pressure with a gauge and replace the switch if it's bad. Don't drive with true low oil pressure.

issues.t: Water pump coolant leak
issues.sym: Coolant drips or a sweet smell near the front of the engine, low coolant, or the temperature gauge rising.
issues.why: The water pump seal can start to leak.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold. Have the pump inspected and replaced if it's leaking, before it causes overheating.

issues.t: A/C blows warm or cuts out on hot days
issues.sym: The A/C cools poorly, blows hot from some vents, or stops cooling during hot weather and then comes back.
issues.why: Owners report A/C failures that dealers sometimes can't reproduce. Causes can include the compressor, a refrigerant leak or a climate control part.
issues.next: Note when it happens and the outside temperature, then have the A/C pressures and climate controls checked while the problem is happening.

issues.t: Seat back panel loose or seat creaks when turning
issues.sym: The panel on the back of a front seat comes loose, or the seat creaks and wobbles when you turn.
issues.why: A retaining clip on the seat backboard can fail, and the seat tilt mechanism can have play.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about bulletins 19-BD-004G and 20-BD-009G, which replace the clip and add a retaining ring.

issues.t: Driveline vibration on AWD 3.8 models
issues.sym: A vibration through the floor or seat at certain speeds.
issues.why: The angles of the driveshaft on AWD 3.8-liter models can be off, causing vibration.
issues.next: Ask a dealer about bulletin 20-DS-002G, which measures and adjusts the driveshaft angles.

issues.t: Headlights go out or won't dim
issues.sym: The headlights shut off fully or don't respond to the dimmer.
issues.why: Owners report headlight control faults on these cars. The cause isn't confirmed.
issues.next: Have the dealer check the light switch and headlight wiring for codes. Ask whether any recall or bulletin applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Battery keeps going dead
issues.sym: The car won't start or cranks slowly after sitting, even after a new battery.
issues.why: Something keeps drawing power with the car off, or the battery isn't being charged properly.
issues.next: Have a shop test the battery and charging system and measure the power drain with the car off to find what's staying awake.

issues.t: Fuel pump can fail and cut drive power (recall)
issues.sym: The engine stumbles, loses power or stalls while driving and may not restart.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump can fail and stop supplying fuel. Two recalls cover these years.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recalls 23V-630 and 24V-282. The dealer replaces the fuel pump for free.

issues.t: Fuel can leak where the fuel pipe meets the fuel rail (recall)
issues.sym: A gasoline smell from the engine bay or around the car, or wet fuel on the engine.
issues.why: The joint between the fuel pipe and the fuel rail may not be tight, so fuel can leak near hot parts.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 26V-229. The dealer inspects the joint and tightens or replaces the fuel pipe for free. Don't park in a garage if you smell fuel.

issues.t: High-pressure fuel tube can leak (recall)
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell from under the hood.
issues.why: On some early 2.5-liter turbo cars, the tube between the high-pressure fuel pump and the fuel rail may not seal.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 21V-208. The dealer replaces the tube for free.

issues.t: Seat belt pretensioner can burst in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No symptom in normal driving.
issues.why: The front seat belt pretensioners can burst open when they fire in a crash and throw metal pieces into the cabin.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 23V-094. The dealer adds a protective cap for free.

issues.t: Instrument display can go blank (recall)
issues.sym: The digital gauge cluster goes dark while driving, hiding speed, fuel and warning lights.
issues.why: A software error can make the instrument panel display fail. Recalls 25V-105 and 26V-019 cover different years, including the 2026 Electrified G80.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Check your VIN and get the free software update. For 26V-019, Genesis advises turning off HD Radio until the update is done.

issues.t: Charging control unit can fail and cut power (recall)
issues.sym: Warning lights, the 12-volt battery not charging, and possible loss of drive power while driving.
issues.why: The Electrified G80 shares the integrated charging control unit (ICCU) recall with other Hyundai Motor Group EVs. The unit can be damaged and stop charging the 12-volt battery.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 24V-868 and get the free inspection and software update or part replacement.

issues.t: Misfire and check engine light on the 2.5 turbo
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with misfire codes, and the engine may shake or run rough.
issues.why: One or more cylinders misfire on the 2.5-liter turbo. Genesis issued bulletin 25-01-051G on it.
issues.next: Have the codes read soon. A flashing check engine light means pull over and stop driving. Ask the dealer about the bulletin.

issues.t: Check engine light for a lean fuel mixture
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P2096, but the car drives normally.
issues.why: The engine computer on the 3.5-liter turbo can flag the fuel mixture as too lean. Genesis released a software update.
issues.next: Ask a dealer for the engine computer update in bulletin 22-FL-001G.

issues.t: Coolant leaking from the radiator reservoir
issues.sym: Coolant drips under the front of the car, a sweet smell, or the coolant level keeps dropping.
issues.why: The radiator overflow tank can leak.
issues.next: Check the coolant level when the engine is cold. Have the dealer inspect the tank under bulletin 22-01-060G and replace it if needed.

issues.t: Tire sidewall failures on 20-inch wheels
issues.sym: A tire loses air or blows out with no warning, and the sidewall is damaged.
issues.why: Owners report sidewall failures on the low-profile 20-inch tires, often after hitting potholes.
issues.next: Check tire pressure and look at the sidewalls often. Replace any tire with a bulge or cut, and consider carrying a spare or inflator.

issues.t: Panoramic sunroof creaks or rattles
issues.sym: Creaking or rattling from the sunroof over bumps.
issues.why: Parts in the panoramic sunroof can rub or move against each other.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about bulletin 23-BD-014G for the sunroof noise fix.

issues.t: Check engine light from the transmission control module
issues.sym: A check engine light with transmission codes, and sometimes the transmission drops a gear and stays there.
issues.why: The electronic control module (E-module) in the 8-speed automatic can fault.
issues.next: Have the codes read. Dealers use bulletin 23-AT-007G and may replace the E-module.

issues.t: Fuel smell after filling up
issues.sym: A strong fuel smell after refueling or after fuel system repairs, sometimes with a check engine light.
issues.why: Owners report fuel odors; causes include a gas cap or vapor system leak, overfilling, or a seal not sealing after repair.
issues.next: Don't top off past the first click. Have the dealer check for leaks and check recall 26V-229 for your VIN.

issues.t: Hum or whine from the rear differential
issues.sym: A humming or whining noise from the rear at certain speeds when speeding up or slowing down.
issues.why: The rear differential lock nut can loosen.
issues.next: Ask the dealer about bulletin 23-DS-004G, which tightens the nut or replaces parts if needed.

issues.t: A/C cools poorly from a refrigerant leak
issues.sym: The A/C doesn't get the cabin cold, especially on hot days.
issues.why: Refrigerant can leak from the evaporator core, or from seal washers at the A/C lines that were damaged by foreign chemicals.
issues.next: Have the A/C checked for leaks. Ask the dealer about bulletins 25-HA-002G and 25-01-019G.

issues.t: Horn stops working
issues.sym: The horn doesn't sound.
issues.why: The horns are mounted flat, so water collects and ruins them. This affects the Electrified G80 too.
issues.next: Get it fixed soon. Bulletin 25-BE-014G replaces the horns and mounts them upright.

issues.t: Battery drains while parked
issues.sym: The 12-volt battery is weak or dead after sitting.
issues.why: A communication error keeps the touch control panel from going to sleep, so it slowly drains the battery.
issues.next: Have the battery tested, and ask the dealer about bulletin 25-01-090G.

issues.t: Genesis Connected Services stop working
issues.sym: Remote features, the app or emergency services stop working.
issues.why: Network dropouts, and a software timer flaw that can shut down the telematics unit after one year.
issues.next: Ask the dealer for the telematics software update in bulletins 25-01-057G and 26-01-012G.

issues.t: Adaptive cruise brakes or speeds up unexpectedly
issues.sym: With cruise control or driver assists on, the car brakes hard for no reason or speeds up on its own.
issues.why: Owners report unexpected braking and acceleration. Dealers have not been able to reproduce it, and the cause isn't confirmed.
issues.next: Be ready to take over and turn off cruise if it acts up. Report it to the dealer and to NHTSA with dates and details.
